name: ASML
description: ASML makes the machines that print the circuit patterns onto silicon wafers using light, and is the sole global supplier of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems, the technology required to manufacture the most advanced logic and memory chips. It earns revenue from selling new lithography systems (EUV and deep ultraviolet/DUV) to foundries, memory makers and IDMs, plus a growing recurring revenue stream from servicing and upgrading its large installed base of previously sold machines ("Installed Base Management"). Because EUV tools are a gating technology for Moore's Law, ASML sits at a uniquely powerful point in the semiconductor supply chain, selling machines that can cost well over $100-400 million each to a small number of the world's most advanced chipmakers.

businessLines.name: EUV systems
businessLines.description: Extreme ultraviolet lithography systems (NXE platform and newer High-NA EXE platform), used for the most advanced logic and memory nodes; ASML is the sole global supplier of this technology.

businessLines.name: DUV systems
businessLines.description: Deep ultraviolet lithography systems used for mature and mid-range nodes as well as some advanced-node layers; a more competitive market than EUV, though ASML remains the leading supplier by advanced capability.
businessLines.revenueNote: DUV unit shipments fell from 374 systems in 2024 to 279 in 2025; exact DUV-only revenue split not separately broken out in all disclosures reviewed

businessLines.name: Metrology and inspection (R&D/product line within systems)
businessLines.description: Computational lithography and metrology/inspection capability that ASML bundles with or sells alongside its lithography systems to support customers' overall process control.
businessLines.revenueNote: Not separately broken out as standalone revenue in ASML's segment disclosure

businessLines.name: Installed Base Management (net service and field option sales)
businessLines.description: Recurring revenue from servicing, upgrading and selling field options for ASML's large installed base of previously shipped systems.
